question: Will the Japanese Diet enact a law reducing the number of seats in the House of Representatives before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Japanese bills with an agreed majority in both houses, submitted with weeks left in a session, mostly pass; but this bill already failed twice (the 45-seat versions, last one deferred in July 2026). On 28 Oct 2026 LDP, Ishin and DPFP broadly agreed on a 31-seat proportional cut; DPFP gives upper-house majority; LDP Diet affairs chief pledged submission and enactment this session (ends 12 Dec). Main risk is the timeline: drafting, submission and passage in ~6 weeks against opposition delaying tactics, plus possible slippage or a political shock. No human market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Coalition agreement LDP–Ishin (Oct 2025): cut lower house from 465 to <=420 (~10%). (8and.jp, 2026-10-03; NHK)
- A 45-seat automatic-cut bill was submitted by LDP+Ishin and failed in two previous Diet sessions; in July 2026 the LDP and Ishin leaders agreed to defer it and prioritise the Imperial House Law. (Nikkei; nippon.com/Jiji 2026-10-22)
- Lower house election held 8 Feb 2026. The ruling side lacks a majority in the House of Councillors. (Wikipedia; cube-soft/Asahi summary 2026-10-28)
- Extraordinary session convened 5 Oct 2026, scheduled for 69 days to 12 Dec 2026; seat-cut bill named a focal issue. (Mainichi via Yahoo, early Oct 2026)
- 22 Oct 2026: LDP presented a compromise at a nine-party council: cut 31 proportional seats and switch PR allocation from D'Hondt to modified Sainte-Laguë. Parties agreed to reach a conclusion by end of October. (nippon.com/Jiji; Japan Times)
- 26 Oct: DPFP drafted its own 19-seat-cut plan; its internal deliberation on the 31-seat plan was seen as deciding whether the bill passes the upper house. (nippon.com; Sankei via Yahoo)
- 25 Oct: LDP Diet Affairs chief said on NHK the party will submit the bill this session and seek enactment. (Daily Sports 2026-10-25)
- 28 Oct: Ishin and DPFP back the 31-seat plan; the three parties broadly agree, to be formalised 29 Oct, then draft and submit the bill. Reported as securing an upper-house majority. Ishin co-leader Fujita: 'deeply frustrating but we accept.' Several opposition parties remain opposed. (NHK 2026-10-28; Nikkei 2026-10-28; cube-soft 2026-10-28; ANN/ABEMA via Yahoo)
- Status quo: no seat-reduction law enacted yet; the bill is not yet formally submitted as of 28 Oct.
- Resolves off passage by both chambers (promulgation not needed), not enforcement or the next election.
- Event window: now -> 31 Dec 2026; the session ends 12 Dec unless extended. As of 28 Oct, ~38 of 69 session days remain.
- Searched, absent: Diet deliberation calendar or vote dates for the bill; which party chairs the relevant upper-house committee; any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker market (none found).

calls.reasoning: Status quo before today: the 45-seat cut bill had been stalled twice (the late-2025 extraordinary session and the 2026 special session), carried over into the Oct 5 to Dec 12 extraordinary session. The upper house was the obstacle: the LDP and Ishin lack a majority there, and the opposition would not cooperate in committee. On Oct 28, 2026 the LDP, Ishin and the DPFP agreed on a compromise cutting 31 proportional seats. The DPFP's votes give the coalition an upper-house majority. Nikkei and others report passage this session is now highly likely. A party-leaders sign-off and bill submission are planned for Oct 29. Remaining risks: under 7 weeks to draft and pass the bill through both chambers (the session can be extended); opposition delaying tactics; LDP internal resistance; competing priorities like the consumption tax cut and the Imperial House Law, which already displaced this bill in June; and possible coalition friction. No human prediction market was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Background: the LDP-Ishin coalition agreement (Oct 2025) required a roughly 10% cut to House of Representatives seats. The LDP and Ishin submitted a 45-seat cut bill in Dec 2025 (Japan Times, 2025-12-05). It did not pass in the 2025 extraordinary session.
- 2026 special session: the bill was resubmitted (nippon.com, 2026-06-24). The opposition refused committee cooperation. LDP and Ishin leaders agreed to put the Imperial House Law first and dropped passage that session; the bill carried over (Nikkei, Jul 2026).
- The current extraordinary session opened Oct 5, 2026 and runs 69 days, to Dec 12, 2026 (Jiji/Nikkei, late Sep 2026). Seat reduction and the consumption tax cut are the headline issues. Extensions are possible under Diet rules but none has been announced.
- Sanin Chuo (2025-09-25) headline: "Seat reduction is a focus for the third time; pushing it through forcefully could reignite confrontation." Sankei memo (pre-session): seat reduction may stall again, with 'resistance forces' inside the LDP too.
- Oct 28, 2026 (NHK/ANN/Nikkei/KSB): the LDP, Ishin and the DPFP agreed in electoral-system talks on an LDP compromise cutting 31 proportional seats, down from 45. The DPFP joined after its ideas, such as a unified proportional ballot, were included. The DPFP deputy leader called it 'a difficult choice'.
- Plan: formal sign-off at a three-party meeting on Oct 29, then joint drafting and submission of the bill this session with the aim of enacting it. Nikkei says the DPFP's support gives the ruling side an upper-house majority and makes passage this session highly likely.
- Opposition criticism: Communist Party member Yamazoe calls the shifting figures (Ishin 45, LDP 31, DPFP 19) unprincipled (J-CAST).
- Resolution: requires passage by both chambers before 2027-01-01. Promulgation and the date the cut takes effect do not matter.
- Event window: now through 2026-12-31 per the criteria. As of Oct 28 about 64 days remain, and the scheduled session end (Dec 12) is about 45 days away.
- Searched for but not found: the bill's submission date or committee schedule; any human prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi; none found); upper-house committee chair allocations.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same facts: the Oct 28 three-party agreement on the 31-seat cut, the DPFP giving an upper-house majority, a session scheduled to end Dec 12 with extension possible, two prior failures, and no market. Their probabilities (0.79-0.80) differ only by judgment on timeline and slippage risk. No factual dispute needed settling; the unknowns (submission date, upper-house committee chair) were missing in all three dossiers and cannot be resolved without web access. A firm cross-chamber majority plus a public enactment pledge makes passage likely, but a short window and a history of slippage justify about a 20% failure chance. I independently land at 0.80.
